name: Lateral meniscus posterior root
description: Tibial attachment of the lateral posterior horn in the posterior intercondylar area, just posteromedial to the lateral tibial eminence and in front of the PCL. A low-signal band sloping down and medially on posterior coronal images, as one to three fascicles with thin fat between them.

normal_values.root_center_to_lateral_tibial_eminence_a: about 5 mm posteromedial (cadaver); about 9 mm on 7 T MRI
normal_values.root_zone: the attachment plus the adjacent 1 cm of meniscus

variants_pitfalls: How far medial: some roots insert on the slope of the medial tibial eminence (22% of single roots at 7 T), so lateral meniscal tissue beside the PCL on notch sagittal images can be normal; tissue continuing up to the medial femoral condyle is a meniscofemoral ligament.
A two-peaked root with fat between fascicles on coronal images is normal, not a tear.

Root tears accompany about 10–15% of ACL tears and are uncommon without one. Single signs are insensitive; calling a tear on any one of cleft, truncated triangle or ghost meniscus found 79–84% with 90–95% specificity.
Extrusion is a weak clue laterally (23% of root tears), as an intact meniscofemoral ligament may hold the meniscus; normal position does not exclude a tear.
